title: Trump's 'art of the deal' is nowhere to be seen with Iran
summary: 美国总统特朗普试图为他亲手发起的美伊战争寻找体面收场,但这位自诩的「谈判大师」却屡屡破坏自己的谈判。文章指出,特朗普违背了他自己在《交易的艺术》中提出的核心原则——绝不显得急切——而伊朗通过封锁霍尔木兹海峡掌握了真正的筹码;一场旨在颠覆德黑兰政权的战争反而强化了伊朗的地缘杠杆。
full_text:
For weeks, Donald Trump has tried to find a way to end the war he started with Iran – a deal that would allow him to declare victory and move past the conflict before it causes severe damage to the global economy and sinks Republican chances in the US midterm elections. But the self-proclaimed master dealmaker can't seem to stop sabotaging his own negotiations or to acknowledge that Iran is now in a better position to demand concessions than it was before the war.

Over the Memorial Day holiday, Trump skipped his eldest son's wedding in the Bahamas and canceled plans to spend the weekend at his New Jersey golf club. The last-minute changes heightened speculation that Trump was ready to unveil a deal to end the war. Trump then announced that he would hold a cabinet meeting on Wednesday at Camp David, the presidential compound in Maryland that has been the site of historic diplomatic summits and pronouncements. But that meeting was moved back to the White House, as it became clear that Trump had not been able to close a deal he could announce with great fanfare at Camp David.

Why has an agreement eluded the business titan who wrote (with a ghostwriter) the bestselling 1987 book The Art of the Deal?

Trump admires strongman leaders and is loth to project any sign of weakness – and he's afraid of reaching a deal with Iran that makes him look weak. The president is also sensitive to criticism that any agreement he negotiates will be worse for the US than the 2015 nuclear deal between Iran and six world powers, which was brokered by Barack Obama's administration. In 2018, during his first term, Trump unilaterally withdrew Washington from that agreement, setting in motion events that led to the current conflict.

By starting a war aimed at regime change in Iran, Trump cornered himself into mostly bad options. Even by the principles set out in his famous book, Trump is at a disadvantage in his negotiations with Tehran. "The worst thing you can possibly do in a deal is seem desperate to make it. That makes the other guy smell blood, and then you're dead," Trump wrote. "The best thing you can do is deal from strength, and leverage is the biggest strength you can have. Leverage is having something the other guy wants."

Trump's main problem is that Iran has more leverage than he does – and Iranian leaders are well aware of that advantage. On 28 February, Trump launched a joint US-Israeli war against Iran, killing the supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, and other top military and political officials within the conflict's early hours. At first, Trump was seduced by the prospect of a quick military victory, as he had achieved in January with a US special forces raid that abducted Venezuela's president, Nicolás Maduro, and whisked him to New York to stand trial.

But, as many analysts had warned, Iran was not like Venezuela, and the Iranian regime would fight hard for its survival, despite the assassination of Khamenei and other senior officials. Tehran retaliated with missile and drone strikes against US military bases across the Middle East, and it targeted the energy infrastructure of its Gulf neighbors. Iran also deployed its most effective economic weapon: it closed the strait of Hormuz, through which more than a fifth of the world's oil supply passed each day.

That closure – along with Iranian attacks on pipelines and gas fields in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates – disrupted the global economy and increased oil prices. (In the US, average gas prices have jumped by 50%, up to nearly $4.50 per gallon, since Trump launched the war.)

Trump and his ally, the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, could not topple the Islamic regime that rose to power after Iran's 1979 revolution. Instead, they ended up strengthening it – by allowing Tehran to deploy its geographic control of the strait of Hormuz into a weapon that could instigate a global energy crisis and a worldwide recession.

After six weeks of intense bombing by the world's most powerful military, Iran continued its blockade of the strait and kept up its missile strikes on Gulf countries and Israel. The US and Iran agreed to a ceasefire on 8 April, but negotiations stalled as Trump vacillated between making a deal and threatening to restart the bombing.

The emerging deal is focused on solving a problem that didn't exist before Trump started this war: fully reopening the strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping so that oil prices can stabilize. Under a draft agreement being circulated to US allies, Washington would also lift its blockade of Iranian ports and allow Tehran to access about $12bn in frozen assets.

And as Trump had done last year when he brokered a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas in Gaza, his administration left some of the thorniest problems (including disarming Hamas and securing Israel's military withdrawal from the Palestinian territory) to later negotiations that never got off the ground.

Once again, Trump seems to be aiming for a limited deal with Iran that defers the most difficult questions to future talks, which could drag out for months or even years. The unresolved issues are likely to include Iran's nuclear program and capabilities; its development of ballistic missiles; and its support for regional militias such as Hamas, Hezbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen. In a video posted on social media on 28 February, Trump laid out those concerns as imminent threats that Iran posed to the US – and the central reason for going to war. None of these issues have been resolved.

In some ways, Iran has emerged stronger after a war intended to decimate its military capabilities. A CIA report sent to Trump earlier this month found that Tehran had managed to retain a significant part of its missile capabilities. The analysis said Iran preserved about 70% of its prewar stockpile of missiles and about 75% of its mobile launchers. The report also concluded that Iran was more resilient than US officials had claimed, and it could survive a naval blockade for months.

Despite his weak position, Trump insists that he will strike a better deal with Iran than the one negotiated by the Obama administration in 2015. That agreement provided Tehran with relief from international sanctions in exchange for limits on its nuclear enrichment. (Iran was allowed to enrich uranium at low levels, enough to run power plants but not to produce a nuclear weapon.) Years after Trump withdrew from the deal, Iran dramatically ramped up its production of uranium enriched to nearly weapons grade, but the UN and other watchdogs found it still had not taken steps to build an actual weapon.

At his cabinet meeting on Wednesday, Trump said he didn't care about the midterm elections and wasn't in a rush to reach a deal. "It's got to be perfect," Trump told reporters, adding: "I didn't do this to get a crummy agreement."

Of course, Trump could have avoided starting a regime-change war that failed, leaving the world to deal with its consequences. Instead, the master negotiator handed Iran a new economic weapon – and more leverage to extract a favorable deal.

annotations_vocab.definition: to deliberately destroy, damage, or obstruct something, especially for political or military advantage
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自法语 sabot(木鞋)+ -age,据传 19 世纪法国工人在抗议中把木鞋扔进机器以破坏生产,故词义引申为「蓄意破坏」。注意发音保留法语 /ʒ/ 音(类似 measure 中的 s)而非英语 /dʒ/。名词形式同形 sabotage(破坏行为);从事者为 saboteur /ˌsæbəˈtɜː/。常被误读为 /ˈsæbətaʒ/,正确重音在首音节。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式偏书面用语,新闻、政治评论高频。常见搭配:sabotage negotiations/talks/efforts/peace process。本文 sabotaging his own negotiations 这种「破坏自己谈判」的用法极具讽刺意味,是 opinion writing 中常见的修辞策略。比 undermine 更强调主动、刻意的破坏行为。

examples.text: Hardliners on both sides have repeatedly sabotaged efforts to revive the peace process.

annotations_vocab.definition: a thing that is granted, especially in response to demands; something yielded in a negotiation
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 concedere(con- 一起 + cedere 让出),即「共同让出」。注意三个常见义项分流:外交/谈判语境中是「让步」(make concessions);商业语境中是「特许经营权」(a coffee concession at the airport);学生场景中可指「优惠票价」(student concessions)。动词形式 concede(承认、让步)与名词意义相通。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,外交、谈判、政治评论核心术语。常见搭配:demand/make/extract/wring concessions from sb;major/minor/significant concessions。IELTS 写作中讨论国际关系、谈判时必备。本文 in a better position to demand concessions 是国际新闻报道的固定表达。

examples.text: Brussels refused to make further concessions on fishing rights during the trade talks.

annotations_vocab.definition: the forming of theories or conjectures without firm evidence; also: investment in stocks/property in the hope of gain but with the risk of loss
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 speculari(观察、侦察),与 spectacle、inspect 同源。词根 spec- 表「看」。两大义项分流:新闻语境中常指「猜测、揣测」(speculation about/that...);金融语境中指「投机交易」(currency speculation)。动词 speculate 同样兼有两义。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,新闻报道高频。常见搭配:fuel/heighten/spark/dampen speculation;widespread/intense speculation;speculation that + 从句。本文 heightened speculation 是新闻写作套语,意为「加剧/激起了人们的猜测」,IELTS 写作中描述舆论反应时非常实用。

examples.text: The CEO's sudden resignation fuelled speculation about the company's financial health.

annotations_vocab.definition: to publicly show or announce something for the first time; to remove a covering from
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 由 un-(去除)+ veil(面纱)构成,字面意为「揭开面纱」,引申为「首次正式公布」。区分近义词:reveal(揭示,语气一般)、disclose(披露,常用于本应保密的信息)、unveil(隆重首次公开,多用于产品发布、政策出台、雕像揭幕)。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,新闻和商业报道高频。常见搭配:unveil a plan/policy/strategy/product/statue。本文 unveil a deal 指「正式公布一项协议」,带有隆重、有仪式感的暗示。Apple 发布新品、政府公布预算都常用此词。

examples.text: The chancellor will unveil her budget to parliament on Wednesday.

annotations_vocab.definition: a short, loud piece of music played on brass instruments to introduce something important; an elaborate public display of attention
annotations_vocab.chinese: (铜管)号角声;隆重的宣传;大张旗鼓
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自法语 fanfare,本义为铜管乐器吹奏的号角声(常用于宫廷仪式宣告国王驾临)。引申为比喻义「隆重的宣传声势」,常见固定搭配 with great fanfare(大张旗鼓地)。与 without fanfare(悄无声息地)构成一对反义表达,在新闻写作中非常常见。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式偏书面,新闻评论常用。固定搭配:with (great/much) fanfare;without fanfare;amid fanfare。本文 announce with great fanfare 是「高调宣布」的标准说法,IELTS 写作描述某政策/产品高调登场时可直接套用。

examples.text: The new electric car was launched with great fanfare in Shanghai last week.

annotations_vocab.definition: to escape from or avoid (someone or something), typically in a skillful way; (of an idea or fact) to fail to be grasped or remembered by someone
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 eludere(e- 出 + ludere 玩、戏弄),原意「戏耍着逃脱」。注意两层义项:具体义为「躲避追捕」(elude the police);抽象义为「(目标、答案)无法企及」(success has eluded him / the cause eludes scientists)。本文 eluded the business titan 用的是抽象义——「协议躲开了这位大亨」即「他无法达成协议」,这是英语 opinion writing 中非常文学化的修辞。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式书面用词,文学、新闻评论高频。常见搭配:elude capture/justice/sb's grasp/understanding;A has eluded B(B 一直未能获得 A)。比 escape 更文雅、更暗含「狡黠地、长期地躲开」之意。IELTS 写作中讨论「某目标长期未能实现」时极佳。

examples.text: A definitive cure for the disease has eluded researchers for over a century.

annotations_vocab.definition: to arrange or negotiate (an agreement or deal) between two or more parties
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 由名词 broker(经纪人、中间商)动词化而来。名词源自古法语 brocour(代理人)。动词化后专指「居间斡旋促成协议」,主语通常是第三方(国家、调解人)。注意被动用法极常见:a deal brokered by X(由 X 促成的协议)。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,国际新闻报道核心动词。常见搭配:broker a deal/ceasefire/peace agreement/truce;a deal brokered by + 调解方。本文 brokered by Barack Obama's administration 是国际报道的标准表达。比 negotiate 更强调「第三方居中调解」的角色,而非自己作为一方参与。

examples.text: Qatar and Egypt have repeatedly brokered ceasefires between Israel and Hamas.

annotations_vocab.definition: in a way that involves only one group or country, without the agreement of others
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 由 uni-(单一)+ lateral(边、侧)+ -ly 构成,字面「只有一边」。对立词族非常重要:bilateral(双边的)、multilateral(多边的)、trilateral(三边的)。形容词 unilateral 与本词共用同一词根。国际关系语境中,unilateral action 常带贬义,暗示绕开盟友/国际共识。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,国际政治、外交报道核心副词。常见搭配:unilaterally withdraw/declare/impose/decide/act。本文 unilaterally withdrew Washington 强调特朗普绕开盟友单方面退出协议的争议性。IELTS 写作讨论国际事务时不可或缺。

examples.text: Russia was condemned for unilaterally annexing the territory in defiance of international law.

annotations_vocab.definition: to force (a person or animal) into a place or situation from which it is hard to escape
annotations_vocab.chinese: 把……逼入绝境;使陷入困境
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 由名词 corner(角落)动词化:「把人逼到角落里」即「让人无路可退」。本文反身用法 cornered himself into 极妙——「特朗普把自己逼进了……」,这种「自己把自己逼入绝境」的表达比 trapped himself 或 left himself with no choice 更生动形象,带视觉画面感。另一相关短语 back into a corner 含义相同。
annotations_vocab.usage: 中性偏书面,新闻评论常用。常见搭配:corner sb into doing sth;be cornered;corner the market(垄断市场,另一义项)。本文 cornered himself into mostly bad options 是 opinion 写作典范,IELTS 写作中批评某决策让自己陷入被动时可套用。

examples.text: By making so many public promises, the prime minister has cornered himself into an unsustainable position.

annotations_vocab.definition: the power to influence a person or situation to achieve a particular outcome; the use of borrowed capital for (an investment)
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 由 lever(杠杆)+ -age 构成。物理学概念「杠杆作用」隐喻引申为「以小博大的谈判筹码」。注意英美发音差异:英音首音节 /liː/,美音 /le/。本文中作为谈判术语反复出现(leverage is the biggest strength;has more leverage),是国际谈判、商业评论的核心词汇。动词化使用也越来越常见:leverage technology(撬动/善用技术)。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,商业、政治、外交核心术语。常见搭配:gain/have/lose/exert leverage over sb;use sth as leverage;significant/considerable leverage。比 power 或 influence 更具体——强调「在谈判中可以拿来交换的筹码」。IELTS 写作和考研英语高频。

examples.text: China's control of rare-earth supplies gives it significant leverage in trade negotiations.

annotations_vocab.definition: to attract someone powerfully into doing something they should not do, often by promising rewards; to entice or tempt
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 seducere(se- 离开 + ducere 引导),即「引开正路」。除了为人熟知的「勾引」义,在政治和商业语境中广泛用作「被诱惑、被吸引」(常用被动 be seduced by)。本文 was seduced by the prospect of 是 opinion 写作的高级表达,暗示当事人被一个看似诱人却虚幻的前景所迷惑——比 was attracted by 多了一层「事后被证明是错觉」的批评意味。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,文学和评论性写作常用。常见搭配:be seduced by + 名词(常为诱人但有风险的事物如 power, profits, simplicity, the prospect of);seduce sb into doing。IELTS 写作批评某种思维盲点时极佳。

examples.text: Investors were seduced by the prospect of quick returns and ignored the obvious risks.

annotations_vocab.definition: to take someone away illegally by force or deception; to kidnap
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 abducere(ab- 离开 + ducere 引导),即「带走」。与 kidnap 含义接近,但 abduct 更正式、更书面化,常用于新闻和法律语境;kidnap 更口语化,且常暗含勒索目的。名词形式 abduction(绑架)、abductor(绑架者)。在生理学中还有「外展肌」义项(将身体部位远离中线)。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,新闻和法律语境。常见搭配:abduct sb at gunpoint;abduct and hold hostage;alleged abduction。比 kidnap 更适合严肃新闻报道。

examples.text: Three aid workers were abducted by armed militants near the Sudanese border.

annotations_vocab.definition: to take or move (someone or something) somewhere suddenly and quickly
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 原义为「快速搅拌」(厨房用具 whisk 即「打蛋器」),引申为「快速移动、迅速带走」。带画面感和速度感,通常搭配 to / off to / away to + 地点,暗示「不容拒绝地迅速送往某处」。本文 whisked him to New York 比 took him to New York 多了「快速、强制、戏剧化」的色彩。
annotations_vocab.usage: 中性偏书面,新闻报道常用以渲染戏剧性。常见搭配:whisk sb to safety/hospital/the airport;be whisked away by helicopter。文学性较强,IELTS 写作中描述「被迅速带走」的场景时可用以提升表达。

examples.text: The injured president was whisked to hospital in an armoured ambulance.

annotations_vocab.definition: to make an attack or assault in return for a similar attack; to take revenge
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 retaliare(re- 回 + talis 同样的),字面「同样地回敬」。与 talion(同态复仇,如「以眼还眼」)同源。注意搭配:retaliate against sb(对某方进行报复)、retaliate with sth(用某手段反击)、retaliate by doing sth(通过……进行报复)。名词形式 retaliation,形容词 retaliatory(报复性的,如 retaliatory tariffs 报复性关税)。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,国际政治、军事、商业报道高频。常见搭配:retaliate against / with / by;swiftly/promptly/in kind retaliate;threaten to retaliate。比 take revenge 更正式、更适合严肃语境。IELTS 写作讨论国际冲突、贸易战时必备。

examples.text: Beijing has vowed to retaliate against any new US tariffs with measures of its own.

annotations_vocab.definition: to move (troops or equipment) into position for military action; to bring into effective use
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自法语 déployer(展开,de- 反 + ployer 折叠),军事原义为「展开兵力」,即把折叠的队列铺开。引申到一般语境为「有策略地调用、运用」(deploy resources/arguments/strategy)。在科技语境中又指「上线、发布」(deploy software/an app)。本文 deployed its most effective economic weapon 是新闻写作的典型用法。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,军事、政治、科技报道高频。常见搭配:deploy troops/forces/weapons;deploy resources/skills/tactics。比 use 更正式、更强调「有计划地部署」。IELTS 写作中可替换 use 提升表达。

examples.text: NATO will deploy additional troops to the eastern flank in response to the threat.

annotations_vocab.definition: to bring about or initiate (an action or event), typically something undesirable; to incite someone to do something
annotations_vocab.chinese: 煽动;挑起;发起(常含贬义)
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 instigare(in- 进入 + stigare 刺激),与 stick(刺)同根。带强烈贬义色彩,暗示「煽动、挑起某种不良行为/事件」。区分与 initiate(中性的「发起」)、provoke(挑衅引发反应)的差异:instigate 更强调幕后主使或刻意挑起。名词 instigation(教唆)、instigator(煽动者)。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,新闻、法律、政治评论高频。常见搭配:instigate violence/riots/a crisis/proceedings;at the instigation of sb(在某人的怂恿/教唆下)。IELTS 写作批评某行为「引发严重后果」时极佳。

examples.text: The opposition accused the government of instigating the protests to discredit them.

annotations_vocab.definition: to overbalance or cause to overbalance and fall; to remove (a government or leader) from power
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自 top(顶部)+ 频率后缀 -le,字面「使顶部倾倒」,即「使倒下」。具体义为「倒塌」(the vase toppled over);政治语境中常用比喻义「推翻政权」(topple a regime/government/dictator),是国际新闻报道的核心动词。比 overthrow 更口语化、更具画面感(「推倒」)。
annotations_vocab.usage: 中性偏书面,政治新闻高频。常见搭配:topple a regime/government/leader/dictator;be toppled from power。本文 topple the Islamic regime 是国际报道固定表达。IELTS 写作讨论政变、政权更替时必备。

examples.text: Mass protests eventually toppled the country's long-ruling autocrat.

annotations_vocab.definition: an act of sealing off a place to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 由 block(阻挡)+ -ade(法语来源的名词后缀,表示行为或结果,如 parade、masquerade)构成。区分:embargo(贸易禁运,经济手段)vs blockade(封锁,常含军事手段)vs sanction(制裁,广义)。可作名词(impose a blockade)也可作动词(blockade a port)。本文中三处出现,既指海上封锁也指经济封锁。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,军事、国际新闻核心词。常见搭配:impose/lift/break a blockade;naval/economic/total blockade;blockade a port/city。IELTS 写作讨论国际冲突、人道主义危机时常用。

examples.text: The UN called for the immediate lifting of the naval blockade to allow humanitarian aid through.

annotations_vocab.definition: to alternate or waver between different opinions or actions; to be indecisive
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 vacillare(摇摆、晃动)。固定搭配 vacillate between A and B(在 A 和 B 之间摇摆),带有贬义,暗示「优柔寡断、缺乏定见」。与近义词比较:waver(动摇,中性偏弱)、oscillate(物理学的「振荡」,引申为反复变化)、hesitate(犹豫,程度更轻)。vacillate 最强调「反复摇摆、迟迟不决」。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式书面用词,政治评论、人物分析常用。常见搭配:vacillate between A and B;vacillate over/about sth。本文 vacillated between making a deal and threatening to restart the bombing 是 opinion 写作典范,可直接套用批评决策者优柔寡断。

examples.text: The chancellor has vacillated for months between raising taxes and cutting public spending.

annotations_vocab.definition: to stop or cause to stop making progress; to delay deliberately
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 本义为「(发动机)熄火」(the car stalled),引申为「进程停滞」。也可作及物动词「故意拖延」(stall for time 拖延时间)。注意区分 stall(进程停止)和 stop(中性的「停止」):stall 暗示「本应推进却卡住了」。名词义为「畜栏、摊位」,与动词义无关,属同形异源。
annotations_vocab.usage: 中性偏书面,新闻报道常用。常见搭配:talks/negotiations stalled;stall for time;stalling tactics(拖延战术)。本文 negotiations stalled 是国际新闻报道高频套语,IELTS 写作描述谈判/项目陷入停滞时极实用。

examples.text: Climate negotiations stalled after several developing nations walked out in protest.

annotations_vocab.definition: to put off (an action or event) to a later time; to postpone
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 deferre(de- 离开 + ferre 带)。注意 defer 有两个不同义项,词源也不同:义项一「推迟」(defer a decision);义项二「遵从」(defer to sb's judgment 遵从某人判断)——后者源自 differ。名词形式 deferral(延期)、deference(尊重、遵从)。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,法律、商务、政治语境高频。常见搭配:defer a decision/payment/judgement;defer sth to + 时间/会议。本文 defers the most difficult questions to future talks 是外交报道固定表达,意为「把难题留给后续谈判」。IELTS 写作讨论决策拖延、问题搁置时极佳。

examples.text: The board deferred the vote on the merger until next quarter.

annotations_vocab.definition: (of a subject or problem) causing difficulty or controversy; full of thorns
annotations_vocab.chinese: 棘手的;充满困难的;多刺的
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 由 thorn(荆棘、刺)+ -y 构成,本义「多刺的」,比喻义「棘手的」——像被荆棘缠绕般难以处理。最高级 thorniest(最棘手的)在 opinion 写作中极常见。近义词比较:tricky(口语,棘手的)、knotty(打结的,复杂难解)、intractable(顽固难解的,更正式更强)。thorny 形象生动,介于口语和正式之间。
annotations_vocab.usage: 中性偏书面,新闻、评论常用。常见搭配:a thorny issue/problem/question/topic;the thorniest of issues。本文 the thorniest problems 是 opinion 写作高频套语。IELTS 写作中替换 difficult 提升表达。

examples.text: Immigration remains one of the thorniest political issues facing the new government.

annotations_vocab.definition: about to happen; impending
annotations_vocab.chinese: 即将发生的;迫近的(常含负面意味)
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 imminere(in- 上方 + minere 突出),字面「悬在头顶」,故引申为「迫在眉睫」。常带负面色彩,多用于威胁、危险、灾难等(imminent threat/danger/collapse)。区分易混词:eminent(杰出的)、immanent(内在的)——三者拼写极易混淆,考研英语常考。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,新闻评论高频。常见搭配:imminent threat/danger/attack/collapse/arrival;pose an imminent threat。本文 imminent threats that Iran posed to the US 是政治和军事报道的固定表达。IELTS 写作中替换 about to happen 提升正式度。

examples.text: Scientists warned that the eruption appeared imminent and called for immediate evacuation.

annotations_vocab.definition: to kill, destroy, or remove a large proportion of; to drastically reduce
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 decimare(deci- 十),原义为古罗马军法「每十人处死一人」(对哗变部队的惩戒),即「十一抽杀律」。现代英语中词义已大大放宽,泛指「大规模毁灭」(远超原义的 10%)。语言纯化论者曾反对这种语义漂移,但当代用法已被词典认可。常见于军事、生态、产业讨论。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,新闻评论高频。常见搭配:decimate the population/army/industry/economy;be decimated by。本文 decimate its military capabilities 是军事报道标准表达。IELTS 写作中替换 destroy 提升正式度,适用于描述行业、生态、人口被严重削弱。

examples.text: The new tariffs have decimated the country's once-thriving textile industry.

annotations_vocab.definition: able to recover quickly from difficulties; (of a material) able to spring back into shape
annotations_vocab.chinese: 有韧性的;有复原力的;抗压的
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 源自拉丁语 resilire(re- 回 + salire 跳),字面「弹回」,本义指材料的弹性,引申为人、系统、组织的「心理韧性、抗压能力」。近年成为心理学和管理学热门术语。名词形式 resilience(韧性、复原力)是近 20 年新闻和学术写作激增的高频词,IELTS 写作核心词汇。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,心理学、管理学、社会评论高频。常见搭配:resilient economy/system/community/individual;remarkably/surprisingly resilient。本文 more resilient than US officials had claimed 是分析报告的标准表达。IELTS 写作讨论应对挑战、可持续发展时极佳。

examples.text: Small businesses have proved remarkably resilient in the face of the prolonged recession.

annotations_vocab.definition: a large accumulated stock of goods or materials; to accumulate a large stock
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 由 stock(库存)+ pile(堆)构成的复合词,字面「库存堆」。多用于战略、军事、能源、医疗等关键资源的「储备」,而非一般商品库存。可名可动:作名词 a stockpile of missiles(导弹储备);作动词 stockpile vaccines(囤积疫苗)。近义词 reserve 更书面,stockpile 更具体强调「成堆累积」。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式用词,军事、能源、公共卫生报道高频。常见搭配:nuclear/missile/oil/strategic stockpile;a stockpile of + 名词;stockpile (sth) for emergencies。IELTS 写作讨论资源储备、应急管理时必备。

examples.text: The government is rapidly building up its strategic stockpile of critical minerals.

annotations_vocab.definition: (informal) of poor quality; unpleasant; lousy
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 来源于 crumb(面包屑)+ -y,字面「碎屑般的、不值钱的」,口语色彩浓厚。属于美式英语口语词,常出现在引用名人讲话或新闻特稿中以保留说话者的语气。本文出现在特朗普直接引语中("I didn't do this to get a crummy agreement"),记者保留这个口语词正是为了真实呈现其讲话风格——这本身就是 quoted speech 的写作技巧。
annotations_vocab.usage: 口语/非正式,英语母语者日常常用。常见搭配:a crummy job/hotel/movie/deal;feel crummy(感觉不舒服)。IELTS 口语 part 2 描述糟糕经历时可用,但不要在正式写作中使用——理解即可。

examples.text: He complained the hotel was crummy and demanded a refund.

annotations_vocab.definition: (also spelled 'loath') reluctant; unwilling
annotations_vocab.linguistics: 古英语词,现代英语保留作为正式书面词。两种拼写并存:loth(英式偏好)和 loath(更常见),发音相同。固定句式 be loth/loath to do sth(不愿做某事)。注意区分极易混淆的同形/近形词:loathe(动词,/ləʊð/,憎恶);loathsome(形容词,令人厌恶的)。词义和发音都不同。
annotations_vocab.usage: 正式书面用词,英国主流媒体常用(Guardian/Economist/FT)。固定句式:be loth/loath to + 动词原形。比 reluctant/unwilling 更文雅、更书面化。在 opinion writing 中常用以分析人物心理动机,本文 is loth to project any sign of weakness 是典型用法。IELTS 写作中分析人物或国家行为动机时可提升表达。

examples.text: Central banks are loath to cut interest rates while inflation remains stubbornly high.

annotations_phrases.definition: the skill of negotiating and making favorable agreements (originally the title of Trump's 1987 book)
annotations_phrases.chinese: 交易的艺术(特朗普 1987 年同名畅销书)
annotations_phrases.linguistics: 本是特朗普 1987 年出版的自传/商业书书名,后成为媒体语境中的文化符号。「the art of + N」是一个高产构词模式:the art of war、the art of conversation、the art of compromise,源自孙子兵法英译标题的影响。本文标题 Trump's 'art of the deal' is nowhere to be seen 借用书名做反讽——「连他自己鼓吹的『艺术』都看不见踪影」,是 opinion writing 中典型的「以子之矛攻子之盾」修辞。
annotations_phrases.usage: 适用于新闻评论、人物分析。常用以引用、反讽或批评。IELTS 写作可借鉴这种「引用对方原话/理念再反驳」的论证结构。

examples.text: His 'art of the deal' approach has yielded few concrete results so far.

annotations_phrases.definition: someone who calls himself a great negotiator (used skeptically or ironically)
annotations_phrases.chinese: 自封的谈判大师(常含讽刺意味)
annotations_phrases.linguistics: self-proclaimed 是 opinion 写作核心修饰语,意为「自封的、自称的」,几乎总带怀疑或讽刺色彩——记者用它暗示「这个头衔是他自己给自己的,不一定属实」。同类常见搭配:self-proclaimed expert/genius/savior/leader。master dealmaker(谈判大师)是 master + N 构词模式,master 作前置定语表「精通……的人」。
annotations_phrases.usage: 新闻评论核心套语,表达保留态度。IELTS 写作中需要批评某人自我标榜时极佳。比 self-styled 略微更书面。

examples.text: The self-proclaimed reformer has done little to actually challenge entrenched interests.

annotations_phrases.definition: to claim success and stop dwelling on an issue (often used when the actual outcome is ambiguous)
annotations_phrases.chinese: 宣布胜利然后翻篇(常暗指实际未必成功)
annotations_phrases.linguistics: declare victory 字面「宣布胜利」,与 move past(把……抛在身后)搭配后形成政治叙事套路:无论实际结果如何,先宣称胜利然后转移话题——这是政治传播学中著名的「declare victory and go home」策略。本文用此短语暗示特朗普寻找的不是真胜利,而是可包装成胜利的台阶,极具批判力度。
annotations_phrases.usage: 政治、商业评论高频,带分析性。IELTS 写作讨论政客/企业「摆姿态、不解决根本问题」时极佳。

examples.text: The administration is keen to declare victory on inflation and move past the issue before the election.

annotations_phrases.phrase: in a better position to demand concessions
annotations_phrases.definition: in a stronger negotiating stance from which to ask the other side to yield
annotations_phrases.chinese: 处于更有利的地位来要求对方让步
annotations_phrases.linguistics: be in a (better/stronger/weaker) position to do sth 是商业、外交、政治写作的核心句式,字面「处于……位置去做……」,即「具备了做……的条件/优势」。比 be able to / can 更精准,强调相对的力量对比。demand concessions from sb(向某方要求让步)是外交报道固定搭配。
annotations_phrases.usage: 正式书面,新闻评论高频。IELTS 写作 Task 2 讨论国际谈判、商业博弈、政策博弈时必备句式。

examples.text: With record-low unemployment, workers are now in a better position to demand higher wages.

annotations_phrases.definition: with a lot of publicity and excitement, often disproportionate to the substance
annotations_phrases.linguistics: 固定副词短语,与 announce / launch / unveil / introduce 等动词搭配。常带保留态度——记者用此短语时往往暗示「场面大于内容」。其反义短语 without fanfare(悄无声息地)同样常见,两者构成 opinion 写作中常用的修辞对比。
annotations_phrases.usage: 新闻评论高频套语。IELTS 写作描述某政策/产品高调登场时直接套用。

examples.text: The reform was announced with great fanfare but quietly shelved months later.

annotations_phrases.definition: to start a process or chain of events that will continue without further input
annotations_phrases.chinese: 引发(连锁反应);使……开始运转
annotations_phrases.linguistics: 字面「使……进入运动状态」,源自牛顿力学的隐喻,强调「一旦发动便会自行发展、难以中止」。常用搭配:set in motion a chain of events / a process / reforms。本文 setting in motion events that led to the current conflict 是历史叙事的标准句式,将一个决策与其长远后果连接起来,非常有力。
annotations_phrases.usage: 正式书面,历史叙事和政治分析高频。IELTS 写作分析「某决策引发了一系列后果」时极佳。

examples.text: The fall of Lehman Brothers set in motion the global financial crisis.

annotations_phrases.phrase: deal from strength / deal from a position of strength
annotations_phrases.definition: to negotiate when you have advantages that the other side wants or needs
annotations_phrases.chinese: 从强势地位进行谈判;以实力谈判
annotations_phrases.linguistics: deal from + 抽象名词 是谈判术语,deal 在此为「打交道、谈判」之义(同 dealmaker)。短语强调「先有筹码,后入谈判桌」。其反义短语 deal from weakness 或 negotiate from a position of weakness 同样常用,opinion 写作中常以此对比分析谈判格局。
annotations_phrases.usage: 外交、商业谈判核心术语。IELTS 写作 Task 2 讨论国际关系、商业博弈、劳资谈判时必备。

examples.text: Beijing prefers to deal from strength, waiting until economic conditions shift in its favour.

annotations_phrases.definition: to sense that an opponent is weakened and become more aggressive
annotations_phrases.chinese: 嗅到血腥味;察觉对手虚弱并趁机进攻
annotations_phrases.linguistics: 比喻自鲨鱼/猛兽闻血而至,生动形象。在谈判、政治、商业语境中比喻「对手嗅到你的弱点便会步步紧逼」。本文出自特朗普书中原话,与上下文中的 desperate 形成因果链:显得急切→对方嗅到血腥→你就输了。形象化表达在 opinion 写作中能极大提升感染力。
annotations_phrases.usage: 口语和书面均可,新闻评论常用。IELTS 写作中作为比喻插入可大幅提升表达生动度。

examples.text: Once short-sellers smell blood, the share price can collapse within days.

annotations_phrases.definition: (of a plan, project, or negotiation) to fail to start successfully or make any progress
annotations_phrases.linguistics: 源自飞机起飞的隐喻:无法离地即无法运行。固定搭配,常用否定形式 never got off the ground / fail to get off the ground。本文 negotiations that never got off the ground 描述谈判从未真正展开,opinion 写作中分析「政策/谈判/项目失败」时的高频用法。
annotations_phrases.usage: 正式与口语均可,新闻评论常用。IELTS 写作和口语描述失败的项目时极实用。

examples.text: The proposed merger never got off the ground due to regulatory concerns.

annotations_phrases.definition: to extend or prolong unnecessarily over a long period
annotations_phrases.linguistics: drag 本义「拖、拽」,drag out 引申为「使……拖延」。本文 could drag out for months or even years 是新闻评论批评谈判/官司/项目久拖不决的固定表达。与 drag on(继续拖下去,不及物)用法略有不同:drag out 强调「被刻意拖延」的色彩。
annotations_phrases.usage: 中性偏书面,新闻评论高频。IELTS 写作分析「问题久拖不决」时极佳。

examples.text: The court case has been dragged out for years by repeated appeals.

annotations_phrases.definition: the replacement of one government or ruling system by another, often through external intervention
annotations_phrases.linguistics: 国际政治核心术语,21 世纪初因伊拉克战争而被广泛使用。regime 在政治语境中常含贬义,暗指「专制的、不正当的政权」(与中性的 government 不同)。本文 a war aimed at regime change in Iran 和 regime-change war 反复出现,是国际政治评论的关键概念。注意 regime-change 作前置定语时需加连字符。
annotations_phrases.usage: 国际政治、新闻评论核心术语。IELTS 写作讨论国际干预、主权、外交时必备。

examples.text: Critics warned that pursuing regime change without a plan for what comes next would destabilise the region.

annotations_phrases.definition: to increase or expand significantly, often quickly
annotations_phrases.chinese: 大幅提升;加快/加大(产量、力度)
annotations_phrases.linguistics: ramp 本义为「斜坡」,ramp up 比喻「沿斜坡上升」,引申为「快速提升」。常见搭配:ramp up production/efforts/pressure/sanctions/output/capacity。其反向短语 scale back(削减、收缩)同样高频,opinion 写作中常以此对比分析「加大/收缩」的策略变化。
annotations_phrases.usage: 商业、政治、军事评论高频。IELTS 写作描述「显著扩大规模/力度」时可替换 increase 提升表达。

examples.text: Pharmaceutical companies have ramped up production of the vaccine to meet global demand.

annotations_phrases.definition: having a level of purity sufficient for use in nuclear weapons
annotations_phrases.chinese: 武器级(铀);可用于制造核武器的纯度
annotations_phrases.linguistics: 核武器和能源报道的核心术语,uranium enriched to weapons grade 指铀-235 浓度达到 90% 以上(可制造核武器),而民用核反应堆只需 3-5% 的低浓缩铀。weapons-grade 也常引申为比喻义,形容「最高等级、最危险/极致的」(weapons-grade stupidity 极致的愚蠢)。
annotations_phrases.usage: 国际新闻、科技报道核心术语。IELTS 写作 Task 2 讨论核扩散、能源安全时必备。

examples.text: Inspectors detected uranium enriched to near weapons grade at the facility.

annotations_sentences.sentence: But the self-proclaimed master dealmaker can't seem to stop sabotaging his own negotiations or to acknowledge that Iran is now in a better position to demand concessions than it was before the war.
annotations_sentences.translation: 但这位自封的谈判大师似乎既无法停止破坏自己的谈判,也无法承认伊朗现在比战前更有底气要求让步。
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:主句 the self-proclaimed master dealmaker can't seem to stop ... or to acknowledge ...; 两个并列不定式宾语 to stop sabotaging / to acknowledge that ...; 宾语从句 that Iran is now in a better position to demand concessions than it was before the war; 比较结构 in a better position ... than it was。语法分析:can't seem to do 是一个貌似简单实则微妙的句型,字面「似乎无法做到……」,语气比 can't do 更委婉、更带分析性,常用于 opinion 写作避免过于断言;not stop doing 和 not acknowledge 由 or 并联,共享否定词 can't,体现作者对特朗普「既不行动也不承认」的双重批评;in a better position to do sth 是商务/外交核心句式,后接不定式说明「具备做什么的优势」。修饰成分:self-proclaimed 前置形容词带强烈讽刺色彩,暗示「这个头衔是他自己给自己加的」;own 强调「他自己的」谈判却被他自己破坏,形成自相矛盾的张力;now 与 before the war 形成时间对比,凸显战争反而强化了对手筹码。
grammar_points: can't seem to do 委婉否定
or 并联两个不定式共享否定
in a position to do sth 句式
than + 从句的比较结构
self-proclaimed 讽刺性形容词
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作中批评某人「既不行动又不承认错误」的双重失败时套用:[Subject] can't seem to stop [doing X] or to acknowledge that [事实 Y]. 这个并列结构能在一句话里完成两层批评,非常凝练。self-proclaimed + 头衔 是引入反讽的高效修饰语。

annotations_sentences.sentence: The last-minute changes heightened speculation that Trump was ready to unveil a deal to end the war.
annotations_sentences.translation: 这些最后一刻的变动加剧了外界的猜测——特朗普即将公布一项结束战争的协议。
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:主句 The last-minute changes heightened speculation; 同位语从句 that Trump was ready to unveil a deal; 不定式作目的状语 to end the war。语法分析:heightened speculation that 是新闻写作核心套语,heighten 比 increase 更精准地强调「加剧、升级」(从已有水平进一步提高);that 引导的同位语从句解释 speculation 的具体内容(注意是同位语从句而非定语从句,因为 that 不在从句中担任成分,只起连接作用);to unveil 用 unveil 而不用 announce 体现作者的精确用词——unveil 暗示「首次正式公布」的隆重感,与下一段 announce with great fanfare 形成呼应。修饰成分:last-minute 复合形容词(连字符连接)修饰 changes,强调突发性;to end the war 是不定式作 deal 的后置定语,说明协议的目的。
grammar_points: heighten + speculation 高级搭配
同位语从句 vs 定语从句的区分
last-minute 复合形容词
不定式作后置定语和目的状语
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作中报道/分析「某事件引发外界猜测」的标准句式:[事件/变动] heightened speculation that [具体猜测]. 比 made people guess 高级得多,且符合英文新闻报道的语感。同位语从句解释抽象名词内容是 academic writing 的核心技巧。

annotations_sentences.sentence: Why has an agreement eluded the business titan who wrote (with a ghostwriter) the bestselling 1987 book The Art of the Deal?
annotations_sentences.translation: 为什么一项协议会让这位写下(由代笔者执笔的)1987 年畅销书《交易的艺术》的商界巨头束手无策?
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:修辞性疑问句; 主句 Why has an agreement eluded the business titan; 定语从句 who wrote ... the bestselling 1987 book The Art of the Deal; 括号插入语 (with a ghostwriter)。语法分析:用修辞性疑问句作为段落开头是 opinion writing 的经典手法,既引出讨论又表态(本句暗示「他确实办不到」);has eluded 现在完成时强调「至今仍未达成」;elude 选词极妙——把「协议」拟人化,仿佛它在「躲避」特朗普,带有戏谑色彩;the business titan 是 Trump 的同位描述(epithet),记者用这种「头衔式称谓」既避免重复又带评价色彩;插入语 (with a ghostwriter) 是典型的「在称赞中暗刺一刀」的写法——表面承认书是他写的,却立刻补充「找人代笔」,削弱其权威性,这是 opinion writing 的高级讽刺技巧。修饰成分:bestselling 强调书的影响力,1987 体现时间久远(暗示「过气」),三层修饰共同烘托后续转折。
grammar_points: 修辞性疑问句引出论点
现在完成时表「至今未……」
elude 拟人化用法
epithet 同位描述
括号插入语的讽刺功能
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作 introduction/body 段中可借鉴这种结构提出反问引发思考:Why has [目标/解决方案] eluded [本应能做到的人/组织] who [显赫资历/承诺]? 修辞性疑问句 + 资历对比 = 引出后续论证的高效套路。括号插入语补充削弱性细节是 opinion writing 的精妙技巧。

annotations_sentences.sentence: Trump admires strongman leaders and is loth to project any sign of weakness – and he's afraid of reaching a deal with Iran that makes him look weak.
annotations_sentences.translation: 特朗普崇拜强人领袖,不愿流露任何示弱的迹象——而且他害怕与伊朗达成一项让自己显得软弱的协议。
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:并列分句通过破折号连接; 分句 1: Trump admires ... and is loth to project ...(两个并列谓语 admires / is loth to); 分句 2: he's afraid of reaching a deal with Iran that makes him look weak; 定语从句 that makes him look weak。语法分析:破折号在 opinion 写作中常用于「补充强调」,比逗号更突出地引出递进结论——前半解释他的「人格倾向」,破折号后揭示这种倾向导致的具体「行为」;be loth to do sth 是正式书面句型,比 be reluctant to 更文雅,适合人物心理分析;project 在此为「投射、展示出(某种形象)」之义,project an image / a sign of strength 是商务/政治写作的核心搭配;that makes him look weak 是限制性定语从句修饰 deal,说明他害怕哪一类协议。修饰成分:any sign of weakness 中 any 强调「任何一丝」,凸显其极端敏感;strongman 是政治学术语,特指威权主义独裁者(俄罗斯/土耳其/匈牙利式领导人),带分析色彩。
grammar_points: 破折号连接递进分句
be loth to do sth 正式句式
project + 抽象名词 高级搭配
that 引导限制性定语从句
strongman 政治学术语
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作分析人物或决策者心理动机的高级句式:[Subject] admires [价值观/类型] and is loth to project [对立特质] – and [由此导致的具体行为]. 破折号引出从「心理」到「行为」的因果链,比 because 更有节奏感。be loth to 替换 be reluctant 提升正式度。

annotations_sentences.sentence: In 2018, during his first term, Trump unilaterally withdrew Washington from that agreement, setting in motion events that led to the current conflict.
annotations_sentences.translation: 2018 年,在他的第一个任期内,特朗普单方面让华盛顿退出了那项协议,由此引发了一系列最终导致当前冲突的事件。
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:主句 Trump unilaterally withdrew Washington from that agreement; 时间状语 In 2018; 同位语 during his first term(进一步限定时间); 现在分词短语作结果状语 setting in motion events; 定语从句 that led to the current conflict。语法分析:用 Washington 代指「美国政府/美国」是新闻写作的转喻(metonymy)手法,既避免重复 the US 又显得专业;现在分词短语 setting in motion events ... 作结果状语,把「退出协议」与「引发后续事件」的因果关系一气呵成地表达,比另起一句更紧凑;set in motion 是国际报道的固定搭配,源自牛顿力学的隐喻,强调「一旦启动便不可逆转」;that led to the current conflict 是限制性定语从句,把 8 年前的决策与今天的战争直接挂钩,这是历史叙事中 retrospective causation(回溯性因果)的核心写法。修饰成分:unilaterally 副词凸显「绕开盟友」的争议性;first term 暗示「这是反复的、可预测的行为模式」。
grammar_points: Washington 转喻代指国家
现在分词作结果状语
set in motion 固定搭配
定语从句连接历史决策与当下后果
副词 unilaterally 政治批判色彩
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作分析「某历史决策导致深远后果」的经典句式:In [年份], [主语] [decisive action], setting in motion events that led to [当前局面]. 这个句式将历史决策与当下问题直接挂钩,非常适合 Task 2 的因果分析。用首都名(Washington/Beijing/Brussels)代指国家是新闻英语的成熟手法,可显著提升表达专业度。

annotations_sentences.sentence: By starting a war aimed at regime change in Iran, Trump cornered himself into mostly bad options.
annotations_sentences.highlight_key: By starting a war aimed at
annotations_sentences.translation: 通过发动一场旨在更迭伊朗政权的战争,特朗普把自己逼入了几乎全是糟糕选项的境地。
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:主句 Trump cornered himself into mostly bad options; 介词短语 By starting a war(方式状语,说明「通过……」); 过去分词短语 aimed at regime change in Iran(后置定语修饰 war)。语法分析:By + 动名词 表示手段/方式,是英文表达「通过做某事」的核心结构,比 Through 更口语化但同样地道;cornered himself into 是反身用法,「把自己逼进……」,这种「自食其果」的修辞在 opinion 写作中非常有力——比 ended up with bad options 多了「主动造成」的批判力度;aimed at + N 是 aim 的被动式作后置定语,常用于描述目的明确的行动(a policy aimed at reducing poverty);mostly 副词修饰 bad options,带分析性的诚实态度(承认并非「全部」糟糕,但「大多数」如此),避免极端化反而更可信。修饰成分:regime change 政治术语;mostly 体现作者的论证克制。
grammar_points: By + 动名词 表方式手段
过去分词短语作后置定语
反身代词 himself 强调自食其果
aimed at 表目的的高级搭配
mostly 限定词增强可信度
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作中批评某决策导致自陷困境的精准句式:By [doing X], [Subject] cornered himself/herself into [负面后果]. 反身用法 cornered himself 是 opinion 写作的「点睛之笔」,直接套用可大幅提升论证力度。avoiding 极端化的副词 mostly/largely/predominantly 是高分写作的体现——避免绝对化表述更显客观。

annotations_sentences.sentence: At first, Trump was seduced by the prospect of a quick military victory, as he had achieved in January with a US special forces raid that abducted Venezuela's president, Nicolás Maduro, and whisked him to New York to stand trial.
annotations_sentences.translation: 起初,特朗普被速战速决的军事胜利前景所诱惑——正如他 1 月份通过一次美军特种部队突袭所取得的成果:那次行动绑架了委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗,并将他迅速押解至纽约接受审判。
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:主句 Trump was seduced by the prospect; 介词宾语 of a quick military victory; 方式从句 as he had achieved in January(类比上一次成功); 介词短语 with a US special forces raid; 定语从句 that abducted Venezuela's president, Nicolás Maduro, and whisked him to New York to stand trial(两个并列谓语 abducted / whisked)。语法分析:这是本文最复杂的「悬挂式长句」,通过 as 从句和定语从句不断展开细节;was seduced by 被动语态 + 介词 by 引出「诱惑源」,这种用法带「事后看来是错觉」的批评色彩;had achieved 过去完成时与主句的过去时形成时间纵深(「此前已经成功过」);as he had achieved 中 as 引导方式从句,但巧妙地省略了重复成分(完整形式 as he had achieved [a quick military victory]);that 引导的定语从句修饰 raid,内含两个并列谓语动词(abducted / whisked),通过两个动作勾勒出一次完整的突袭行动;不定式 to stand trial 作目的状语,说明「绑架」的目的。修饰成分:At first 时间副词,与暗含的「后来发现并非如此」形成隐性对比;quick 形容词揭示特朗普的判断错误。
grammar_points: was seduced by 被动 + by 引出诱惑源
as 引导方式从句 + 省略
过去完成时 had achieved 表先时
定语从句内两个并列谓语
不定式作目的状语
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作中描述「某人被错误的成功经验所误导」的长句模板:At first, [Subject] was seduced by [诱人前景], as [Subject] had achieved [类似成功] with [具体案例] that [详细行动描述]. 这种「主句 + as 类比从句 + 定语展开」结构能在一句话里完成事件描述 + 类比 + 细节铺陈三层信息,是 opinion 写作的高级句式。

annotations_sentences.sentence: Iran also deployed its most effective economic weapon: it closed the strait of Hormuz, through which more than a fifth of the world's oil supply passed each day.
annotations_sentences.highlight_key: Iran also deployed its most effective
annotations_sentences.translation: 伊朗还动用了它最有效的经济武器:封锁了霍尔木兹海峡——全球每日有超过五分之一的石油供应从这里通过。
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:主句 Iran also deployed its most effective economic weapon; 冒号引出具体说明 it closed the strait of Hormuz; 非限制性定语从句 through which more than a fifth of the world's oil supply passed each day(介词 + 关系代词结构)。语法分析:冒号在英文中常用于「先说概括,再展开具体」,本句先抛出 most effective economic weapon 制造悬念,再用冒号揭晓答案,是新闻写作的「引人入胜」技巧;through which 是「介词 + 关系代词」结构,等同于 which ... through(从这里通过),这种把介词前置的写法比 which ... through 更正式优雅,是学术和新闻英语的标志;a fifth 表示 1/5(也可写作 one-fifth),分数表达英文中常用 a/one + 序数词的形式(a third, a half, two-thirds 等)。修饰成分:most effective 最高级强调「这是最厉害的一招」;each day 副词短语强调数据的日常持续性,凸显冲击力。
grammar_points: 冒号引出具体说明
介词 + 关系代词 (through which)
非限制性定语从句
分数表达 a fifth
副词 each day 强调日常持续
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作中「先抛悬念再揭晓」+「数据支撑」的高分句式:[Subject] deployed [its most effective tool]: [具体做法], through which [数据/事实]. 冒号制造节奏感,「介词 + which」结构提升学术性。同时该句也展示了如何用分数(a fifth/half/third)和频率(each day/year)让数据更具冲击力。

annotations_sentences.sentence: Once again, Trump seems to be aiming for a limited deal with Iran that defers the most difficult questions to future talks, which could drag out for months or even years.
annotations_sentences.highlight_key: Once again, Trump seems to be
annotations_sentences.translation: 再一次,特朗普似乎正在追求一项有限的对伊协议——把最棘手的问题推给未来的谈判,而那些谈判可能拖延数月甚至数年。
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:主句 Trump seems to be aiming for a limited deal with Iran; 时间副词 Once again(开头点出「重复模式」); 定语从句 1: that defers the most difficult questions to future talks; 非限制性定语从句 2: which could drag out for months or even years(用逗号隔开,补充评论)。语法分析:Once again 开头是 opinion writing 的「pattern recognition」(模式识别)修辞,暗示「这是他一贯的做法,并非偶然」,极具批判力;seems to be doing 是「主观判断 + 现在进行时」的组合,既表达分析又保留余地;两个定语从句构成层层递进——that defers... 解释这项协议的性质,which could drag out 进一步评论这种性质会带来的后果;defer ... to future talks 是外交报道核心搭配「把……推给后续谈判」;could drag out 用情态动词 could 表「可能性」,比 will 更克制可信。修饰成分:limited 修饰 deal 带贬义,暗示「不彻底」;months or even years 用渐进式列举强化拖延的可能时长。
grammar_points: Once again 模式识别修辞
seems to be doing 主观判断 + 进行时
限制性 vs 非限制性定语从句
defer A to B 外交搭配
情态动词 could 表克制可能性
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作 conclusion 段中批评「重复性的不彻底做法」的强力句式:Once again, [Subject] seems to be [doing X] that defers [核心问题] to [later时机], which could drag out for [时长]. Once again 暗示这是一贯模式,两个定语从句层层展开后果,非常适合作 Task 2 结论段的批判性总结。

annotations_sentences.sentence: Despite his weak position, Trump insists that he will strike a better deal with Iran than the one negotiated by the Obama administration in 2015.
annotations_sentences.translation: 尽管处于不利地位,特朗普仍坚称他将与伊朗达成一项比 2015 年奥巴马政府所谈成的协议更好的协议。
annotations_sentences.breakdown: 句式结构:让步状语 Despite his weak position; 主句 Trump insists that ...; 宾语从句 that he will strike a better deal with Iran; 比较结构 than the one negotiated by the Obama administration in 2015; 过去分词短语 negotiated by ...(修饰 the one)。语法分析:Despite + 名词短语是「让步状语」的高级表达,比 Although + 从句更简洁,适合新闻评论;insists that 选词带有「明知不利仍坚持」的批判色彩——比 says 或 claims 更显「固执」;strike a deal 是商务/外交固定搭配,strike 在此为「敲定、达成」(比 reach 更生动有力);than the one 中 the one 是替代词,指代前文的 deal 避免重复;negotiated by the Obama administration 是过去分词短语作后置定语,等同于省略关系代词的 that was negotiated by。修饰成分:weak position 与 better deal 形成强烈的「现实 vs 妄言」反差,是 opinion 写作的核心修辞策略。
grammar_points: Despite + 名词短语 让步状语
insists that 带批判色彩的引述动词
strike a deal 商务固定搭配
the one 替代避免重复
过去分词短语作后置定语
annotations_sentences.writing_tip: IELTS 写作中批评「与现实不符的承诺」的精准句式:Despite [客观不利条件], [Subject] insists that [他声称的更好结果]. 「让步状语 + 引述动词 insists」组合制造了强烈的「现实-言论」反差,是 opinion writing 的常用修辞武器。strike a deal 替换 reach an agreement 让表达更地道。
